p: Sánchez was born in Santo Domingo on 9 March 1817. His mother, Olaya del Rosario Belén, was a free woman of colour; his father, Narciso Sánchez Ramona, a descendant of slaves, worked in the cattle and meat trade. The parents married only in 1819, which is why he bore his mother's surname before his father's. He was taught first by his mother and then by the Peruvian priest Gaspar Hernández. Juan Pablo Duarte, a classmate, recruited him to La Trinitaria, founded in 1838.

When Duarte and others left the country on 2 August 1843 to escape Haitian persecution, Sánchez, who was ill, stayed behind in hiding and took over the leadership of the movement. On the night of 27 February 1844 his men took the Ozama Fortress, and at the Puerta del Conde, after Matías Ramón Mella fired his blunderbuss, he raised the flag. He presided over the Central Government Board, and assured freed people who had mutinied under Santiago Basora that slavery would not return.

Pedro Santana marched on Santo Domingo and on 12 July 1844 drove the Trinitarios from the board. On 22 August Duarte, Sánchez and Mella were declared traitors and deported for life. He lived as a teacher in Curaçao until an amnesty granted by President Manuel Jimenes in 1848. Back home, he sided with Buenaventura Báez against Santana, was exiled again to Curaçao, returned in August 1856 and became governor of the province of Santo Domingo, and in 1859 was banished a third time, to Saint Thomas.

In 1861 Sánchez formed the Dominican Revolutionary Board and obtained from the Haitian president Fabre Geffrard passage through Haitian territory and weapons for a force of 500 men. He entered through Hondo Valle on 1 June 1861. When Haiti withdrew its support under threat from a Spanish squadron at Port-au-Prince, the expedition turned back. On 20 June Sánchez was ambushed near Hondo Valle by Santiago de Óleo, a former ally, wounded in the leg and groin, and captured.

A war council at San Juan under General Domingo Lazala tried the prisoners; Sánchez, conducting his own defence, asked that he alone be condemned. He was shot at San Juan de la Maguana on 4 July 1861 with some twenty companions, some of whom were finished off with machetes and clubs. Spain withdrew from the country in 1865. Dominicans honour him with Duarte and Mella as a founder of the republic, and the Order of Merit of Duarte, Sánchez and Mella bears his name.

notes: Read in excerpts (the article has 12,000 words and long quoted speeches).

'some twenty companions': the article says a last group of 20 were taken prisoner and lists about nineteen others sentenced to death; it does not give one total of those shot. The editor may prefer 'with his companions'.

The article says his aunt María Trinidad Sánchez was 'tortured and executed by Santana' and later that Santana 'had his aunt and brother murdered'; left out for room, and the brother is not otherwise explained in what I read.
The date of the second exile is not clear in the article (after the executions of 11 April 1855); I gave no date.
The article's tone is strongly partisan for Sánchez; I kept to events.
His age when he took over the movement is given as 25 in the article, which does not fit a birth in March 1817 and late 1843; left out.
